title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Given strings s and t, return the shortest substring of s that contains every character of t (including duplicates). Return an empty string if none exists.

reference.use_case: Finding the shortest span of a document or log that contains every required term, such as a search-result snippet or the tightest time range in which all symptoms of an incident appear.
system_examples: Search snippet generation (e.g. Lucene/Elasticsearch highlighters) — picking a short passage that covers the query terms for result previews
Incident tooling — finding the tightest log time window that contains all required error signatures
Bioinformatics — locating the shortest genomic region that contains a required set of motifs
reference.explanation: Expand the right edge until all required characters are covered, then shrink the left edge while coverage holds, tracking counts in a hash map; this finds the minimum window in O(|s| + |t|) instead of checking all O(n²) substrings. The expand/contract window is the standard tool for coverage queries over streams.
